To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) T cells in the primary follicles are CD4+, and (ii) T cells in human secondary follicles are CD3+ and CD4+ and are also CD5+, CD8+, and CD25+.
the majority of T cells in mouse primary and secondary follicular regions express the CD4+ phenotype, and that the majority of follicular T cells in human lymphoid organs express the CD4- phenotype.
T cells are present within primary and secondary follicular regions of mouse and human peripheral lymphoid tissues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: 1) The phenotype of T cells within the primary follicles of human lymph nodes and spleen, and within the primary and secondary follicular regions of the mouse spleen.
the expression of T cell antigencs by cells in mouse primary and secondary follicular structures.
the study of the expression of cell surface markers in normal and neoplastic lymphoid cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
T cells are not present in the primary follicles of the spleen and lymph nodes.
the follicles of both mouse and human lymph nodes, spleen and Peyer's patches contain a small number of T cells, the vast majority being B cells.
T cells do not normally enter the follicles of primary and secondary follicle in mouse or human lymphoid organs and that the few T cells which are found within follicles are not normally there.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
T cell antigens are expressed by a significant number of cells within these B cell compartments.
T cells are not present in follicles of normal lymphoid organs and that the occasional T cell found in follicles is probably a contaminant from the surrounding T cell region.
the T cells in these regions are not the same population as those in the T cell domains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the majority of T cells in these B cell regions do not express T cell markers and therefore are unlikely to be T cells.
T cells can be found within the follicles of human and mouse lymphoid organs.
T cells are rare in mouse and human follicles, and those T cells that are present are not typical helper T cells.
